words.gloss: for the service of the gods

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारे उस सर्वोच्च बल की मैं स्तुति करता हूँ, देवों की सेवा के लिए, जब तुम ओज से वृत्र को मारते हो, हे शक्ति के स्वामी।
english: I praise that highest strength of yours, O Indra, for the service of the gods, when you slay Vṛtra with might, O lord of power.
notes: The '~' in yaddha~si is the candrabindu for anusvāra: yad haṃsi. upamām is taken as 'highest, foremost'; 'nearest' is also possible. śacī is rendered 'power' (śacīpate). upamām (f.) cannot agree with neuter śavaḥ; it is read adverbially ('in the highest degree').
lines_deva: गृणे तदिन्द्र ते शव उपमां देवतातये
यद्धँसि वृत्रमोजसा शचीपते
lines_iast: gṛṇe tadindra te śava upamāṃ devatātaye
yaddha~si vṛtramojasā śacīpate

words.gram: name of a demon, m. acc. sg.
pres. part. caus. √randh, m. nom. sg.

hindi: जिसके मद में तुम उस शम्बर को दिवोदास के वश में करते हुए: हे इन्द्र, यह वही सोम तुम्हारे लिए निचोड़ा गया है; पिओ।
english: In whose exhilaration you, making that Śambara subject to Divodāsa: this is that Soma, O Indra, pressed for you; drink.
notes: randhayan is printed as given; as a present participle ('subduing, delivering up') it has no 'you' of its own, which is supplied from the address to Indra. The translation keeps the participle; tyat does not agree in gender with śambaram (tyam would be expected) and is read simply as 'that'. Śambara and Divodāsa are names; nothing further is imported.
lines_deva: यस्य त्यच्छम्बरं मदे दिवोदासाय रन्धयन्
अयँ स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब
lines_iast: yasya tyacchambaraṃ made divodāsāya randhayan
aya~ sa soma indra te sutaḥ piba

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे प्रिय, हे सदा विजयी, हे न छिपने वाले, हमारे पास आओ; पर्वत के समान सब ओर से विशाल, तुम आकाश के स्वामी हो।
english: Come to us, O Indra, O dear one, O ever-victorious, O unconcealable one; broad on every side like a mountain, you are the lord of heaven.
notes: Line 2 has no verb; 'you are' is supplied. gadhi is taken as an imperative of ā-√gā 'come' (Vedic gadhi).
lines_deva: एन्द्र नो गधि प्रिय सत्राजिदगोह्य
गिरिर्न विश्वतः पृथुः पतिर्दिवः
lines_iast: endra no gadhi priya satrājidagohya
girirna viśvataḥ pṛthuḥ patirdivaḥ

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे सबसे बलवान, जो सबसे अधिक सोम पीने वाला मद प्रकट होता है, जिससे तुम भक्षक को नीचे गिरा देते हो, उसी को हम माँगते हैं।
english: The exhilaration that, most Soma-drinking, is perceived, O Indra, O most mighty, by which you strike down the devourer, that we beg for.
notes: nyā3triṇaṃ: ni + atriṇam sung with a pluta (the figure 3), given as its own word; it is not translated. The '~' in ha~si is the candrabindu for anusvāra. īmahe is read as 1 pl. of √ī 'seek, ask'; the object 'that' is the exhilaration. soma-pātama is taken as an adjective of madaḥ.
lines_deva: य इन्द्र सोमपातमो मदः शविष्ठ चेतति
येना हँसि न्या३त्रिणं तमीमहे
lines_iast: ya indra somapātamo madaḥ śaviṣṭha cetati
yenā ha~si nyā3triṇaṃ tamīmahe

hindi: हे शक्तिशाली आदित्यो, हमारी सन्तान और वंशजों के लिए जीने को वह और भी लम्बी आयु दो।
english: O mighty Ādityas, grant to our offspring and descendants that longer life, to live.

text_flags.why: possible: the usual comparative is drāghīyas; drādhīyas may be a genuine Sāmaveda variant

notes: drādhīya is read as the Vedic comparative of dīrgha/drāghīyas 'longer'; the spelling drādhīya is doubtful and is flagged. tuce tunāya are read as dative 'for offspring, for descendants'; their exact sense (child / progeny) is not certain. sa-mahasaḥ is read as 'having greatness / might', or 'of equal might'. 'Our' goes with the offspring (naḥ), as 'for us' is also possible.
lines_deva: तुचे तुनाय तत्सु नो द्राधीय आयुर्जीवसे
आदित्यासः समहसः कृणोतन
lines_iast: tuce tunāya tatsu no drādhīya āyurjīvase
ādityāsaḥ samahasaḥ kṛṇotana

hindi: हे वज्र हाथ में लिए हुए, तुम विपत्तियों के निवारण को जानते हो; दिन-प्रतिदिन तुम शुद्ध करने वाले हो।
english: For you know, O thunderbolt-handed one, the turning aside of calamities; day after day, the bright purifier, [unclear].
notes: parivṛjam is read as 'turning aside, avoidance'; paripadām (gen. pl.) is obscure: 'snares' is only a guess and the iva clause is not firmly construed. No firm reading; the translation is tentative. paripadām iva is left [unclear] in the English and omitted in the Hindi.
lines_deva: वेत्था हि निरृतीनां वज्रहस्त परिवृजम्
अहरहः शुन्ध्युः परिपदामिव
lines_iast: vetthā hi nirṛtīnāṃ vajrahasta parivṛjam
aharahaḥ śundhyuḥ paripadāmiva

hindi: रोग को दूर करो, विफल होने वाले को दूर करो, दुर्मति को दूर भगाओ; हे आदित्यो, हमें संकट से अलग रखो।
english: Drive away disease, drive away the failing one, drive away ill-will; O Ādityas, keep us apart from distress.

text_flags.why: possible: the Ṛgveda parallel reads sridham; stridham may be a variant or a typo

notes: stridham: the Ṛgveda parallel has sridham (sridh 'failure, mishap'); the printed stridham may be a variant or a typo, so the gloss is tentative. a~hasaḥ is aṃhasaḥ (candrabindu for anusvāra). yuyotana (class 3 imperative) is lengthened in the printed yuyotanā.
lines_deva: अपामीवामप स्त्रिधमप सेधत दुर्मतिम्
आदित्यासो युयोतना नो अँहसः
lines_iast: apāmīvāmapa stridhamapa sedhata durmatim
ādityāso yuyotanā no a~hasaḥ

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सोम को पिओ; वह तुम्हें आनन्दित करे, जिसे हे भूरे घोड़ों वाले, पत्थर ने तुम्हारे लिए निचोड़ा है, निचोड़ने वाले की दोनों भुजाओं से भली-भाँति थामा हुआ, घोड़े की तरह।
english: Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it gladden you, the Soma that the stone has pressed for you, O owner of bay horses, well held in the two arms of the presser, like a horse.
notes: haryaśvādriḥ is read as the vocative haryaśva followed by adriḥ 'stone' (nom.); 'arvā' is read as the nominative of arvan, 'like a steed'; the exact construction of 'suyato nārvā' is loose. The '~' in soturbāhubhyā~ is the candrabindu (bāhubhyām).
lines_deva: पिबा सोममिन्द्र मन्दतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः
सोतुर्बाहुभ्याँ सुयतो नार्वा
lines_iast: pibā somamindra mandatu tvā yaṃ te suṣāva haryaśvādriḥ
soturbāhubhyā~ suyato nārvā

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम जन्म से ही सदा शत्रुरहित, नायकरहित और मित्ररहित हो; युद्ध में ही तुम मित्रता चाहते हो।
english: Without a rival, without a leader, without a friend you are, O Indra, by birth, from of old; it is in battle that you seek friendship.
notes: anā is doubtful: it is taken as 'without a leader' (an-ā); the Ṛgveda parallel is usually rendered 'rivalless and friendless', so anā may be an extra negative term or a corruption. yudhedāpitvam = yudhā id āpitvam.
lines_deva: अभ्रातृव्यो अना त्वमनापिरिन्द्र जनुषा सनादसि
युधेदापित्वमिच्छसे
lines_iast: abhrātṛvyo anā tvamanāpirindra januṣā sanādasi
yudhedāpitvamicchase

hindi: जिसने पहले हमारे लिए यह-यह और श्रेष्ठतर वस्तुएँ आगे लाकर दीं, उसकी, हे मित्रो, तुम्हारे लिए मैं स्तुति करता हूँ, इन्द्र की, सहायता के लिए।
english: He who formerly brought us this and that, and the better things: him I praise for you, O friends, Indra, for help.
notes: 'pra vasya ānināya' is read as pra + vasyaḥ + ā-nināya ('brought forth the better'); vasyaḥ may also be read 'wealth'. vaḥ is the enclitic 'for you / to you'.
lines_deva: यो न इदमिदं पुरा प्र वस्य आनिनाय तमु व स्तुषे
सखाय इन्द्रमूतये
lines_iast: yo na idamidaṃ purā pra vasya ānināya tamu va stuṣe
sakhāya indramūtaye

hindi: आओ, हानि मत पहुँचाओ; हे आगे बढ़ने वालो, दूर मत रहो, हे समान उग्र उत्साह वालो; दृढ़ वस्तुओं को भी थामने वालो।
english: Come; do not do harm; O you who set forth, do not stay away, O ardent together; O you who can restrain even firm things.
notes: The addressees are not named in the lines. riṣaṇyata (do not harm / do not be harmed) is uncertain in sense; mā apa sthāta is read as 'do not stand aloof'. yamayiṣṇavaḥ is read as a vocative 'able to hold in check'.
lines_deva: आ गन्ता मा रिषण्यत प्रस्थावानो माप स्थात समन्यवः
दृढा चिद्यमयिष्णवः
lines_iast: ā gantā mā riṣaṇyata prasthāvāno māpa sthāta samanyavaḥ
dṛḍhā cidyamayiṣṇavaḥ

hindi: आओ; यह बूँद के लिए है; हे अश्वों के स्वामी, हे गौओं के स्वामी, हे खेतों के स्वामी, सोम को पिओ, हे सोम के स्वामी।
english: Come; this is for the drop. O lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fields, drink the Soma, O lord of Soma.
notes: 'ayam indave' is awkward: ayam 'this' (Soma) and indave 'for the drop' (indu); the lines do not name Indra, but the epithets are those of a deity addressed. The reading is tentative. The '~' in soma~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra.
lines_deva: आ याह्ययमिन्दवेऽश्वपते गोपत उर्वरापते
सोमँ सोमपते पिब
lines_iast: ā yāhyayamindave'śvapate gopata urvarāpate
soma~ somapate piba

hindi: हे वृषभ, तुम्हारे साथ सहायक के रूप में हम फुफकारते हुए का सामना कर सकें, गौओं वाले जन की सभा में।
english: With you as our ally, O bull, may we answer the snorting one, at the gathering of the people who possess cattle.
notes: prati bruvīmahi is 'speak in reply / against'; the snorting one is not named. 'sa~sthe' is saṃsthe (candrabindu for anusvāra); saṃsthe may also mean 'in the end / in the meeting-place'.
lines_deva: त्वया ह स्विद्युजा वयं प्रति श्वसन्तं वृषभ ब्रुवीमहि
सँस्थे जनस्य गोमतः
lines_iast: tvayā ha svidyujā vayaṃ prati śvasantaṃ vṛṣabha bruvīmahi
sa~sthe janasya gomataḥ

hindi: गौएँ भी समान मन वाली हैं, समान जन्म के कारण; मरुत् भी बन्धुओं वाले हैं; वे एक-दूसरे के कूबड़ चाटते हैं।
english: Even the cows are of one mind, by common birth; the Maruts, being kinsmen, lick one another's humps.
notes: The syntax is loose: gāvaś cid ... samanyavaḥ and marutaḥ sabandhavaḥ are read as two parallel clauses sharing the verb rihate. kakubhaḥ may be 'humps' or 'peaks, quarters'; the comparison is not worked out. Tentative.
lines_deva: गावश्चिद्धा समन्यवः सजात्येन मरुतः सबन्धवः
रिहते ककुभो मिथः
lines_iast: gāvaściddhā samanyavaḥ sajātyena marutaḥ sabandhavaḥ
rihate kakubho mithaḥ

words.gloss: O all-surveying one, O active one

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे सौ शक्तियों वाले, हे सर्वद्रष्टा, तुम हमारे लिए बल और पौरुष लाओ, और सेनाओं को जीतने वाला वीर भी लाओ।
english: You, O Indra, bring us might and manly strength, O hundred-powered one, O all-surveying one; bring a hero who overcomes hosts.
notes: vicarṣaṇe: the form is voc. 'O all-surveying one' (vicarṣaṇi); 'active, bold' is also possible. nṛmṇa~ is nṛmṇam (candrabindu).
lines_deva: त्वं न इन्द्रा भर ओजो नृम्णँ शतक्रतो विचर्षणे
आ वीरं पृतनासहम्
lines_iast: tvaṃ na indrā bhara ojo nṛmṇa~ śatakrato vicarṣaṇe
ā vīraṃ pṛtanāsaham

hindi: अब, हे इन्द्र, हे स्तुतिप्रिय, इच्छा के साथ हम तुम्हारे पास आते हैं, हमने छोड़ा है; जैसे जल के साथ वे जलों के पास पहुँचे।
english: Now indeed, O Indra, O lover of praise, with desire we approach you, we have sent forth; as they have come to water with waters.
notes: kāma is read as kāmaḥ 'desire' (nom.); kāmān 'desires' is possible. The object of sasṛgmahe is not stated and none is supplied. udeva gmanta udabhiḥ is obscure: read as 'like (those) who have come to water with waters'.
lines_deva: अधा हीन्द्र गिर्वण उप त्वा काम ईमहे ससृग्महे
उदेव ग्मन्त उदभिः
lines_iast: adhā hīndra girvaṇa upa tvā kāma īmahe sasṛgmahe
udeva gmanta udabhiḥ

hindi: तुम्हारे गोदुग्ध से मिले, मधुर, आनन्ददायक पर पक्षियों की तरह बैठे हुए हम, हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारी ओर ज़ोर से स्तुति करते हैं।
english: Sitting like birds at your milk-mixed, sweet, exhilarating [unclear], we sing out to you, O Indra.
notes: Line 1 is obscure: go-śrīte 'mixed with milk', madhau 'in the sweet', madire 'in the exhilarating' are loc. singular; vivakṣaṇe is uncertain ('mighty / being carried'). No noun is supplied for the three adjectives; vivakṣaṇe is left [unclear].
lines_deva: सीदन्तस्ते वयो यथा गोश्रीते मधौ मदिरे विवक्षणे
अभि त्वामिन्द्र नोनुमः
lines_iast: sīdantaste vayo yathā gośrīte madhau madire vivakṣaṇe
abhi tvāmindra nonumaḥ

hindi: हे अद्वितीय, हम सहायता चाहने वाले, मानो किसी खम्भे को उठाते हुए, तुम्हें, हे वज्रधारी, अद्भुत को, पुकारते हैं।
english: We, desiring help, like those carrying some pillar, call upon you, O unequalled one, O wielder of the thunderbolt, the wonderful one.
notes: sthūraṃ na kaccid bharantaḥ is read as 'like those carrying some pillar'; the point of the comparison is not given. apūrvya 'unprecedented, unequalled'. vajriñcitra~ is vajrin + citram (candrabindu for anusvāra); citram may also be read as an adjective of the help, not of Indra.
lines_deva: वयमु त्वामपूर्व्य स्थूरं न कच्चिद्भरन्तोऽवस्यवः
वज्रिञ्चित्रँ हवामहे
lines_iast: vayamu tvāmapūrvya sthūraṃ na kaccidbharanto'vasyavaḥ
vajriñcitra~ havāmahe

words.gloss: of honey, of the sweet drink
with the bull, with the mighty one

hindi: इस प्रकार वे गौएँ मधुर, विस्तृत मधु का पान करती हैं, जो इन्द्र के साथ चलने वाली हैं, बलवान के साथ शोभा से आनन्दित होती हैं, उत्तम हैं; स्वराज्य के अनुसार।
english: Thus the cows drink of the sweet, abundant honey, those that accompany Indra and rejoice with the mighty bull in splendour, the good ones, according to self-rule.
notes: gauryaḥ is taken as 'cows' (gaurī, a bovine); viṣūvataḥ is obscure ('pervading, wide, abundant'); vasvīḥ 'good, rich'. 'His' is not supplied: anu svarājyam is a refrain, 'according to self-rule'. Tentative.
lines_deva: स्वादोरित्था विषूवतो मधोः पिबन्ति गौर्यः
या इन्द्रेण सयावरीर्वृष्णा मदन्ति शोभथा वस्वीरनु स्वराज्यम्
lines_iast: svādoritthā viṣūvato madhoḥ pibanti gauryaḥ
yā indreṇa sayāvarīrvṛṣṇā madanti śobhathā vasvīranu svarājyam

hindi: इस प्रकार, हे सोम, मद ने ही प्रार्थना को वर्धन बनाया; हे सबसे बलवान, हे वज्रधारी, तुमने अपने बल से पृथ्वी से सर्प को बाहर काट दिया, स्तुति करते हुए, स्वराज्य के अनुसार।
english: Thus indeed, O Soma, the exhilaration made the prayer a strengthening; O most mighty, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with might you cut the serpent out of the earth, chanting, according to self-rule.
notes: soma inmado: in = id 'indeed' + madaḥ (the reading 'soma in made', in the Soma exhilaration, is a possible alternative, which would need the locative made); the sentence division is tentative. niḥ śaśāḥ is obscure (a form of √śas 'cut, strike'); pṛthivyā is read as ablative 'from the earth'. arcan is taken as a participle without a clear subject. 'anu svarājyam' is a refrain. brahma may also be read as the priest (brahmā) as subject of cakāra; the reading 'the exhilaration made the prayer a strengthening' is tentative.
lines_deva: इत्था हि सोम इन्मदो ब्रह्म चकार वर्धनम्
शविष्ठ वज्रिन्नोजसा पृथिव्या निः शशा अहिमर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम्
lines_iast: itthā hi soma inmado brahma cakāra vardhanam
śaviṣṭha vajrinnojasā pṛthivyā niḥ śaśā ahimarcannanu svarājyam

hindi: इन्द्र, वृत्र का संहारक, पुरुषों के द्वारा आनन्द और बल के लिए बढ़ा है; उसी को हम बड़े और छोटे संग्रामों में सहायता के लिए पुकारते हैं; वह वाजों की होड़ में हमारी रक्षा करे।
english: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has grown through men for exhilaration and for strength; him we call for help in the great contests and in the small; may he help us on in the contests for prizes.
notes: taminmahatsvājiṣūtimarbhe = tam it mahatsu ājiṣu ūtim arbhe; mahatsu and arbhe are 'in the great (ones)' and 'in the small (one)', with ājiṣu 'contests'. vājeṣu may also be 'in the prizes'. no'viṣat = naḥ aviṣat.
lines_deva: इन्द्रो मदाय वावृधे शवसे वृत्रहा नृभिः
तमिन्महत्स्वाजिषूतिमर्भे हवामहे स वाजेषु प्र नोऽविषत्
lines_iast: indro madāya vāvṛdhe śavase vṛtrahā nṛbhiḥ
taminmahatsvājiṣūtimarbhe havāmahe sa vājeṣu pra no'viṣat

words.gram: n. nom./acc. sg. (does not agree with māyayā; doubtful reading)

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे पत्थर के धारी, हे वज्रधारी, तुम्हारे ही लिए यह अप्रतिहत वीरता है, जब तुमने उस मायावी पशु को अपनी उसी माया से मार डाला, स्तुति करते हुए, स्वराज्य के अनुसार।
english: To you indeed, O Indra, O wielder of the stone, O wielder of the thunderbolt, belongs irresistible heroic power, when you slew that crafty beast by that craft of yours, chanting, according to self-rule.
notes: 'belongs' is supplied in line 1. tyat in tyanmāyayā is the pronoun 'that' agreeing with māyayā (tyayā expected), so it may stand for tyat as adverbial; the sense 'by that craft of yours' is kept. mṛga 'beast' is not identified.
lines_deva: इन्द्र तुभ्यमिदद्रिवोऽनुत्तं वज्रिन्वीर्यम्
यद्ध त्यं मायिनं मृगं तव त्यन्माययावधीरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम्
lines_iast: indra tubhyamidadrivo'nuttaṃ vajrinvīryam
yaddha tyaṃ māyinaṃ mṛgaṃ tava tyanmāyayāvadhīrarcannanu svarājyam

hindi: आगे बढ़ो, आक्रमण करो, साहस करो; तुम्हारा वज्र रोका नहीं जाता। हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारा बल पौरुष ही है; तुम वृत्र को मारते हो, जलों को जीतते हो, स्तुति करते हुए, स्वराज्य के अनुसार।
english: Go forth, attack, be bold; your thunderbolt is not held back. O Indra, your strength is manly power indeed; you slay Vṛtra, you win the waters, chanting, according to self-rule.
notes: dhṛṣṇuhi is read as an imperative of √dhṛṣ (Vedic -nu- stem); No object is supplied for abhi-ihi. yaṃsate is read as 3 sg. middle 'is held back', the verb ni-√yam. hanaḥ and jayāḥ are read as injunctives with present sense. nṛmṇa~ is nṛmṇam; ya~sate is yaṃsate (candrabindu for anusvāra).
lines_deva: प्रेह्यभीहि धृष्णुहि न ते वज्रो नि यँसते
इन्द्र नृम्णँ हि ते शवो हनो वृत्रं जया अपोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम्
lines_iast: prehyabhīhi dhṛṣṇuhi na te vajro ni ya~sate
indra nṛmṇa~ hi te śavo hano vṛtraṃ jayā apo'rcannanu svarājyam

hindi: जब स्पर्धाएँ उठती हैं, तब साहसी के लिए धन रखा जाता है। मद से टपकते अपने दोनों भूरे घोड़ों को जोतो; किसे मारोगे, किसे धन में स्थापित करोगे? हमें, हे इन्द्र, धन में स्थापित करो।
english: When the contests arise, the prize is set for the bold one. Yoke your two bay horses dripping with exhilaration; whom will you slay, whom will you place in wealth? Place us, O Indra, in wealth.
notes: udīrata is a valid 3 pl. middle (impf./aor.) of ud-√īr, read with present sense 'arise'. 'your' in 'your two bay horses' is supplied. hanaḥ and dadhaḥ are injunctive forms, translated as futures / imperative in the last clause. ka~ is kam (candrabindu).
lines_deva: यदुदीरत आजयो धृष्णवे धीयते धनम्
युङ्क्ष्वा मदच्युता हरी कँ हनः कं वसौ दधोऽस्माँ इन्द्र वसौ दधः
lines_iast: yadudīrata ājayo dhṛṣṇave dhīyate dhanam
yuṅkṣvā madacyutā harī ka~ hanaḥ kaṃ vasau dadho'smā~ indra vasau dadhaḥ

hindi: उन्होंने खाया, आनन्द मनाया और प्रिय को झटक दिया; स्वयं तेजस्वी प्रेरित मेधावियों ने सबसे नई मति से स्तुति की। अब, हे इन्द्र, अपने दोनों भूरे घोड़ों को जोतो।
english: They have eaten, they have rejoiced, they have shaken off the dear ones; the self-radiant inspired ones have praised with the newest thought. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
notes: akṣan is read as an aorist of √ghas 'eat'; the object of ava adhūṣata 'the dear ones' is not named. 'praised' lacks an object; 'you' is the natural one but is not stated. yojā nvindra te harī is a refrain.
lines_deva: अक्षन्नमीमदन्त ह्यव प्रिया अधूषत
अस्तोषत स्वभानवो विप्रा नविष्ठया मती योजा न्विन्द्र ते हरी
lines_iast: akṣannamīmadanta hyava priyā adhūṣata
astoṣata svabhānavo viprā naviṣṭhayā matī yojā nvindra te harī

hindi: हे मघवन्, स्तुतियों को भली-भाँति सुनो, वैसा न हो जाओ; कब तुम हमें सत्य-सुवचन वाला बनाओगे, कब हमारी इच्छा पूरी करोगे? अब, हे इन्द्र, अपने दोनों भूरे घोड़ों को जोतो।
english: Hear the songs well, O bountiful one; do not be thus, as it were. When will you make us possessed of kindly truth, when will you grant our aim? Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
notes: mātathā iva is obscure: read as mā + tathā + iva 'not so, as it were'; a different division (such as māteva) is possible, and the line-1 sentence is tentative. sūnṛtāvat 'possessing kindly truth' (sūnṛtā = pleasant true speech). arthayāsaḥ is read as a causative of √arth 'to seek, grant'; uncertain. 'my' is not supplied: giraḥ is rendered 'the songs'. idyojā = id yojā; the refrain 'yojā nvindra te harī' recurs in 415 and 424.
lines_deva: उपो षु शृणुही गिरो मघवन्मातथा इव
कदा नः सूनृतावतः कर इदर्थयास इद्योजा न्विन्द्र ते हरी
lines_iast: upo ṣu śṛṇuhī giro maghavanmātathā iva
kadā naḥ sūnṛtāvataḥ kara idarthayāsa idyojā nvindra te harī

hindi: चन्द्रमा जलों के भीतर है; सुन्दर पंखों वाला आकाश में दौड़ता है। सोने के किनारों वाली बिजलियाँ तुम्हारे पद-चिह्न को नहीं पातीं। हे दोनों लोक, मेरा यह जान लो।
english: The moon is within the waters; the fair-winged one runs in the sky. The golden-rimmed lightnings do not find your track. Know this of mine, O two worlds.
notes: apsvā3ntarā: apsu + antar + ā with a pluta, the figure 3 given as its own word; the ā is read as a preverb of dhāvate (ā ... dhāvate, 'runs'); 'is' is supplied in the first clause. suparṇa (fair-winged) 'bird' is not identified. vittam me asya is read as 'know this of mine' (me asya, the object is not named). vaḥ is the enclitic plural 'your'.
lines_deva: चन्द्रमा अप्स्वा३न्तरा सुपर्णो धावते दिवि
न वो हिरण्यनेमयः पदं विन्दन्ति विद्युतो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी
lines_iast: candramā apsvā3ntarā suparṇo dhāvate divi
na vo hiraṇyanemayaḥ padaṃ vindanti vidyuto vittaṃ me asya rodasī

hindi: तुम्हारा स्तोता, ऋषि, हे अश्विनो, अत्यन्त प्रिय, बलवान, धन ढोने वाले रथ की ओर स्तुतियों से सेवा करता है; हे मधुमय दोनों, मेरी पुकार सुनो।
english: Your singer, the sage, O Aśvins, attends with praises your dearest chariot, the mighty one that bears wealth; O sweet ones, hear my call.

text_flags.why: possible: ṛśi is not a standard form; ṛṣi (sage) is expected and is read here

notes: 'prati ... ratham' is read with bhūṣati (towards the chariot); the second prati is left in the line as printed and is taken as part of the same governing phrase. 'ṛśi' as printed is not a standard form: read as ṛṣiḥ 'sage' (nom.), flagged as possible. mādhvī is the dual vocative of mādhvī 'sweet, honeyed'. priyatama~ and śruta~ are accusatives in -m (candrabindu).
lines_deva: प्रति प्रियतमँ रथं वृषणं वसुवाहनम्
स्तोता वामश्विनावृशि स्तोमेभिर्भूषति प्रति माध्वी मम श्रुतँ हवम्
lines_iast: prati priyatama~ rathaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vasuvāhanam
stotā vāmaśvināvṛśi stomebhirbhūṣati prati mādhvī mama śruta~ havam

hindi: हे अग्नि, हम तुम्हें, तेजस्वी और अजर को, हे देव, प्रज्वलित करें; जब तुम्हारी वह अधिक प्रशंसनीय समिधा आकाश में दीप्त होती है, तब स्तोताओं के लिए पोषण लाओ।
english: O Agni, may we kindle you, the radiant, unaging one, O god; when that more admirable kindling of yours shines in heaven, bring refreshment to the singers.

text_flags.why: the sense needs yat + ha (when indeed); the u is probably a typing error for a

notes: yuddha is read as yad dha (yat + ha); the printed u is probably a typo for a. 'dyumantaṃ devājaram' is an accusative phrase with 'you' supplied; ā te idhīmahi can also mean 'we kindle for you'. dyavīṣa~ = dyavi + iṣam (candrabindu for anusvāra). panīyasī 'more worthy of praise', rendered as 'more admirable'.
lines_deva: आ ते अग्न इधीमहि द्युमन्तं देवाजरम्
युद्ध स्या ते पनीयसी समिद्दीदयति द्यवीषँ स्तोतृभ्य आ भर
lines_iast: ā te agna idhīmahi dyumantaṃ devājaram
yuddha syā te panīyasī samiddīdayati dyavīṣa~ stotṛbhya ā bhara

hindi: हम तुम्हें होता के रूप में, अग्नि की तरह, सुन्दर रीति से मुड़ी हुई स्तुतियों से वरते हैं, पवित्र ज्वाला वाले, यज्ञों में बिछे कुशासन वाले।
english: We choose you as Hotṛ priest with well-turned praises, like Agni, [unclear], of pure flame, in the sacrifices where the sacred grass is strewn; [unclear].
notes: āgniṃ: ā + agnim as printed (the Ṛgveda parallel begins with agnim). śīram is obscure ('bright, swift' is a guess). The tail 'vi vo made ... vivakṣase' is a refrain that is not clear in sense; vivakṣase is read as 2 sg. of a desiderative of vi-√vah, and vaḥ is the plural 'you'. The same tail occurs in 422. The translation is tentative. English marks śīram and the tail 'vi vo made vivakṣase' as [unclear]; the Hindi leaves them out.
lines_deva: आग्निं न स्ववृक्तिभिर्होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे
शीरं पावकशोचिषं वि वो मदे यज्ञेषु स्तीर्णबर्हिषं विवक्षसे
lines_iast: āgniṃ na svavṛktibhirhotāraṃ tvā vṛṇīmahe
śīraṃ pāvakaśociṣaṃ vi vo made yajñeṣu stīrṇabarhiṣaṃ vivakṣase

words.gloss: O rich in horses and kindly truth

hindi: हे उषा, हे तेजस्वी, आज हमें महान् धन के लिए जगाओ, जैसे तुमने हमें जगाया था, सत्यश्रवा वाय्य के लिए, हे सुजात, हे अश्व और सत्य-सुवचन वाली।
english: Awaken us today, O Dawn, O bright one, for great wealth, as you awakened us for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born one, O rich in horses and kindly truth.
notes: The proper names Satyaśravas and Vāyya are read from the locatives satyaśravasi vāyye (they could also be read as common words 'of true fame', 'in the weaving'); the line does not say who they are. mahe is 'for great (wealth)' agreeing with rāye. divitmatī 'possessing heaven, bright'. sūnṛtā 'kindly bounty / truth'.
lines_deva: महे नो अद्य बोधयोषो राये दिवित्मती
यथा चिन्नो अबोधयः सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसूनृते
lines_iast: mahe no adya bodhayoṣo rāye divitmatī
yathā cinno abodhayaḥ satyaśravasi vāyye sujāte aśvasūnṛte

hindi: हमारे लिए शुभ मन, कौशल और संकल्प को प्रवाहित करो; तब तुम्हारी मित्रता में, रस के मद में, चरागाह में गौओं की तरह आनन्द करते हुए।
english: Waft to us a good mind, skill and resolve; then, in friendship with you, in the exhilaration of the juice, as cows rejoice in pasture, [unclear].

text_flags.why: possible: the Ṛgveda parallel reads raṇan; raṇā may be a Sāmaveda variant

notes: raṇā is doubtful; the Ṛgveda parallel has raṇan ('they rejoice'), so a typo or variant is possible. The tail 'vi vo made ... vivakṣase' is a refrain and its sense is unclear; see 420. bhadram agrees with manaḥ ('a good mind'); skill and resolve are further objects of vātaya. The translation of the second line is tentative.
lines_deva: भद्रं नो अपि वातय मनो दक्षमुत क्रतुम्
अथा ते सख्ये अन्धसो वि वो मदे रणा गावो न यवसे विवक्षसे
lines_iast: bhadraṃ no api vātaya mano dakṣamuta kratum
athā te sakhye andhaso vi vo made raṇā gāvo na yavase vivakṣase

words.gloss: according to his own nature, at will

hindi: संकल्प से महान्, अपनी प्रकृति के अनुसार भयंकर, उसका बल इधर घूम आया है; शोभा के लिए ऊँचे, शिरस्त्राणधारी, भूरे घोड़ों वाले ने दोनों हाथों में लोहे का वज्र धारण किया है।
english: Great by resolve, terrible at his own will, his strength has turned hither; lofty for splendour, [unclear: upākayoḥ], helmeted, owner of bay horses, he has taken the iron thunderbolt in both hands.
notes: The subject is not named; anuṣvadham is 'in accordance with his own nature / at will'. upākayoḥ is obscure (printed upākayorni); read as upākayoḥ + ni with ni belonging to dadhe, giving 'ni dadhe' with 'near / close' left unrendered in the translation. śipri 'helmeted' (or 'with fine jaws / lips') is uncertain. mahā~ is mahān; the 'in both hands' phrase is hastayor vajram āyasam. No identification of the subject is made beyond what the lines state.
lines_deva: क्रत्वा महाँ अनुष्वधं भीम आ वावृते शवः
श्रिय ऋष्व उपाकयोर्नि शिप्री हरिवां दधे हस्तयोर्वज्रमायसम्
lines_iast: kratvā mahā~ anuṣvadhaṃ bhīma ā vāvṛte śavaḥ
śriya ṛṣva upākayorni śiprī harivāṃ dadhe hastayorvajramāyasam

words.gloss: for the yoking of the bay horses (?)

hindi: वही उस बलवान, गौओं को खोजने वाले रथ पर चढ़ता है, जो, हे इन्द्र, भूरे घोड़ों को जोतने के लिए भरे हुए पात्र को पहचानता है। अब, हे इन्द्र, अपने दोनों भूरे घोड़ों को जोतो।
english: He indeed mounts that mighty cow-finding chariot who perceives, O Indra, the full cup for the yoking of the bay horses. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
notes: hāriyojanam is obscure; read as 'for the yoking of the bays', although a place name or a kind of cup are possible. The break in sense between the chariot clause and the cup clause is as printed. pūrṇamindrā: pūrṇam + indra with a lengthened final vowel. vṛṣaṇa~ and pātra~ are accusatives in -m (candrabindu). yojā nvindra te harī is a refrain (see 415, 416).
lines_deva: स घा तं वृषणँ रथमधि तिष्ठाति गोविदम्
यः पात्रँ हारियोजनं पूर्णमिन्द्रा चिकेतति योजा न्विन्द्र ते हरी
lines_iast: sa ghā taṃ vṛṣaṇa~ rathamadhi tiṣṭhāti govidam
yaḥ pātra~ hāriyojanaṃ pūrṇamindrā ciketati yojā nvindra te harī

hindi: मैं उसी अग्नि को मानता हूँ जो वसु है, जिसके घर को गौएँ जाती हैं; उसके घर को तेज़ घोड़े जाते हैं, उसके घर को नित्य बलवान जाते हैं; स्तोताओं के लिए पोषण लाओ।
english: I deem him Agni, who is the good one, to whose home the milch cows go; to his home go the swift horses, to his home the constant strong ones; bring refreshment to the singers.
notes: vasuḥ is read as 'the good one / wealth'; the Ṛgveda parallel reads vasur astaṃ ... as 'the dwelling'. 'his' and 'go' in the second line are supplied from line 1. iṣa~ is iṣam (candrabindu).
lines_deva: अग्निं तं मन्ये यो वसुरस्तं यं यन्ति धेनवः
अस्तमर्वन्त आशवोऽस्तं नित्यासो वाजिन इषँ स्तोतृभ्य आ भर
lines_iast: agniṃ taṃ manye yo vasurastaṃ yaṃ yanti dhenavaḥ
astamarvanta āśavo'staṃ nityāso vājina iṣa~ stotṛbhya ā bhara

hindi: हे देवो, उस मरणशील को न संकट पहुँचता है, न दुर्गति, जिसे एकमत होकर अर्यमा, मित्र और वरुण शत्रुताओं के पार ले जाते हैं।
english: Neither distress nor trouble reaches that mortal, O gods, whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, of one accord, lead beyond hostilities.
notes: devāsaḥ is read as a vocative ('O gods'); some take it as the subject. aṣṭa is taken as 3 sg. aorist of √aś 'reach'. nayati ... ati dviṣaḥ: 'lead beyond hostilities' (compare the refrain in the glossary). tama~ho = tam aṃhaḥ.
lines_deva: न तमँहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यम्
सजोषसो यमर्यमा मित्रो नयति वरुणो अति द्विषः
lines_iast: na tama~ho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyam
sajoṣaso yamaryamā mitro nayati varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ

hindi: हे सोम, मधुर, इन्द्र के लिए, मित्र के लिए, पूषन् के लिए, भग के लिए चारों ओर बहो।
english: Flow forth around, O Soma, sweet, for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, for Bhaga.
notes: bhagāya is read as the name Bhaga (a deity in a list with Mitra and Pūṣan); 'for fortune / share' is possible.
lines_deva: परि प्र धन्वेन्द्राय सोम स्वादुर्मित्राय पूष्णे भगाय
lines_iast: pari pra dhanvendrāya soma svādurmitrāya pūṣṇe bhagāya

hindi: चारों ओर भली-भाँति आगे बहो, वाज जीतने के लिए, बाधाओं को चारों ओर से पार करने वाले; शत्रुओं को पार करने के लिए, ऋण चुकाने वाले की तरह तुम हमारे लिए उठते हो।
english: Flow well forth around for the winning of the prize, overcoming the obstacles on every side; to overcome the hostile ones, you set out for us as one who settles debts.
notes: dviṣastaradhyā = dviṣaḥ taradhyai (dative infinitive 'to overcome'). ṛṇayāḥ is read as 'settling debts' (one who pays back); the force of the phrase is uncertain. paryū ṣu = pari u su.
lines_deva: पर्यू षु प्र धन्व वाजसातये परि वृत्राणि सक्षणिः
द्विषस्तरध्या ऋणया न ईरसे
lines_iast: paryū ṣu pra dhanva vājasātaye pari vṛtrāṇi sakṣaṇiḥ
dviṣastaradhyā ṛṇayā na īrase

hindi: हे सोम, बहो, स्वच्छ होकर; तुम महान् समुद्र हो, देवों के पिता, सब धामों के ऊपर।
english: Flow clear, O Soma, great ocean, father of the gods, over all realms.
notes: 'you are' is supplied; viśvā ... dhāma is read as 'all realms' (n. acc. pl., the pl. dhāmā shortened).
lines_deva: पवस्व सोम महान्त्समुद्रः पिता देवानां विश्वाभि धाम
lines_iast: pavasva soma mahāntsamudraḥ pitā devānāṃ viśvābhi dhāma

hindi: हे सोम, महान् कौशल के लिए बहो, धोए हुए वाजी घोड़े की तरह, इनाम के लिए।
english: Flow clear, O Soma, for great skill, like a washed, prize-winning horse, for the prize.
lines_deva: पवस्व सोम महे दक्षायाश्वो न निक्तो वाजी धनाय
lines_iast: pavasva soma mahe dakṣāyāśvo na nikto vājī dhanāya

hindi: बूँद स्वच्छ होकर बही है, मनोहर, आनन्द के लिए, जलों की गोद में, कवि, सौभाग्य के लिए।
english: The drop has flowed clear, lovely, for exhilaration, in the lap of the waters, the seer, for fortune.
notes: bhagāya is read as 'for fortune (bhaga)'; the name Bhaga is also possible (compare 427).
lines_deva: इन्दुः पविष्ट चारुर्मदायापामुपस्थे कविर्भगाय
lines_iast: induḥ paviṣṭa cārurmadāyāpāmupasthe kavirbhagāya

words.gloss: in the lordship of the contest (samarya)

hindi: हे सोम, तुम्हारे निचोड़े जाने पर हम निश्चय ही आनन्दित होते हैं, संग्राम के महान् स्वामित्व के लिए; हे बहते हुए, तुम वाजों में उतरते हो।
english: Truly, O Soma, we rejoice in you, the pressed one, for the great lordship of the contest; O flowing-clear one, you plunge forth into the prizes.
notes: samaryarājye is obscure (samarya 'contest, assembly' + rājya 'lordship'); the translation keeps both members. suta~ is sutam and vājā~ is vājān (candrabindu). anu ... madāmasi is read as 'we rejoice in accordance with / after'.
lines_deva: अनु हि त्वा सुतँ सोम मदामसि महे समर्यराज्ये
वाजाँ अभि पवमान प्र गाहसे
lines_iast: anu hi tvā suta~ soma madāmasi mahe samaryarājye
vājā~ abhi pavamāna pra gāhase

hindi: वे प्रकट, एक ही नीड़ के पुरुष, रुद्र के युवक और अच्छे घोड़ों वाले कौन हैं?
english: Who are they, the manifest men of one nest, the young men of Rudra, and well-horsed?
notes: ka īṃ is read as 'who (are) they'; kaḥ is singular but the answer is plural. atha is as printed (the Ṛgveda parallel reads adha, the same sense 'then, and'). maryāḥ may be 'mortals' or 'young men'.
lines_deva: क ईं व्यक्ता नरः सनीडा रुद्रस्य मर्या अथ स्वश्वाः
lines_iast: ka īṃ vyaktā naraḥ sanīḍā rudrasya maryā atha svaśvāḥ

hindi: हे अग्नि, उस तुमको आज, घोड़े की तरह स्तुतियों से, शुभ हृदय-स्पर्शी संकल्प की तरह; तुम्हारी भेंटों से हम समृद्ध हों।
english: O Agni, that one today, like a horse, with praises, like an auspicious, heart-touching resolve; may we prosper through your offerings.
notes: The first line has no verb; 'that one' (tam) is the antecedent of a clause not given here, and the verb is not supplied in the English (nor in the Hindi). ohaiḥ is read as 'with carryings / offerings'. bhadra~ is bhadram (candrabindu).
lines_deva: अग्ने तमद्याश्वं न स्तोमैः क्रतुं न भद्रँ हृदिस्पृशम्
ऋध्यामा त ओहैः
lines_iast: agne tamadyāśvaṃ na stomaiḥ kratuṃ na bhadra~ hṛdispṛśam
ṛdhyāmā ta ohaiḥ

hindi: प्रकट होकर मनुष्य, बलवान घोड़े, देव सविता की प्रेरणा में वाज की ओर आ गए हैं; हे घोड़ो, स्वर्ग-गामियों को जीतो।
english: Openly the men, the strong ones, have come to the prize, in the impulse of the god Savitṛ; O horses, win the heaven-going ones.

text_flags.why: possible: agman (3 pl. aorist) is expected with the plural subject; agmam would be 1 pl.

notes: agmaṃ as printed is read as agman (3 pl. aorist 'have come'); agmam could also be 1 pl. 'we have come'. svargā~ arvanto jayata is obscure: svargān is taken as 'heaven-going', with arvantaḥ the vocative 'O horses'; 'win' lacks a clear object. The sense is tentative.
lines_deva: आविर्मर्या आ वाजं वाजिनो अग्मं देवस्य सवितुः सवम्
स्वर्गाँ अर्वन्तो जयत
lines_iast: āvirmaryā ā vājaṃ vājino agmaṃ devasya savituḥ savam
svargā~ arvanto jayata

hindi: हे सोम, द्युम्नवान्, सुन्दर धारा वाले, महान्, भेड़ों के क्रम से पीछे चलने वाले, बहो।
english: Flow clear, O Soma, splendid, with a fine stream, great, following in order among the sheep.
notes: avīnām (of the ewes / sheep) anupūrvyaḥ ('following in due order') is obscure; the reference may be to the wool filter. The translation keeps the literal reading. mahā~ is mahān (candrabindu).
lines_deva: पवस्व सोम द्युम्नी सुधारो महाँ अवीनामनुपूर्व्यः
lines_iast: pavasva soma dyumnī sudhāro mahā~ avīnāmanupūrvyaḥ
